# RoLoRA Report — Expert Review Panel (master review)

This is the consolidated, definitive revision checklist for *"Reproducing and Extending RoLoRA: Alternating Optimization of LoRA for Robust Federated Fine-Tuning"* (Popovici, Iftode, Zele). All findings below survived adversarial verification (one refuted finding dropped). Numbers are taken from `runs/REGISTRY.md` ground-truth logs and the rendered PDF. Where the panel softened or re-scoped a reviewer's original framing, the item is marked **[needs-nuance]** and the corrected framing is given — do not over-correct text the paper already hedges accurately.

---

|---|---|---|---|

**HARD GATE — per-member contributions:** SATISFIED on the report side (a "Team contributions" paragraph is present in §6). Ensure the live presentation also states per-member contributions.

**The single throughline to 12/10:** *Reframe the paper around the one genuinely novel thing it found — an init×schedule interaction (orthogonal-A alone HURTS at 82.94 < 85.10 vanilla, but orth-A+BBA is the best arm at 88.32) — state it honestly as a candidate (PC-RoLoRA), surface the negative orth-alone cell, fix the four credibility-gating defects (baseline collapse explanation, complete/honest 2×2, one consistent error-bar convention + significance statement, and the missing reproducibility audit), and harvest the cheap structural marks (contributions paragraph, repo footnote, appendices, ours-vs-original anchor).* Nothing here requires retracting a claim the paper already hedges; it requires **exposing data the team already has** and **fixing transcription/convention errors**.

## 2. The four cross-cutting issues that gate the grade

### (a) Baseline collapse to chance (~52%) is unexplained and contradicts the original paper — **BLOCKER → corrected to a correctness/explanation fix**

**The defect.** §4.1.2 reports "FedAvg-LoRA and FFA-LoRA stall at 51.9% and 52.0%, respectively, barely above the 50% chance level" and that "neither baseline ever escapes the chance region," framing a ~33pp gap as evidence of RoLoRA's robustness. In the **original** RoLoRA paper these baselines *learn* QNLI well above chance. A baseline pinned at exactly chance is not what lossy averaging predicts (that predicts degraded-but-learning), so as written the comparison reads as either an unargued regime effect or unfair/under-tuned baselines.

**Verified facts.** FedAvg-LoRA lr1e-2 = 51.89; FFA-LoRA lr1e-2 = 51.95; across the **whole** LR sweep {5e-3, 1e-2, 2e-2} both stay ~50–55% while RoLoRA reaches 85.10 at lr1e-2. So the baselines received **identical tuning to the method** and still failed — this rules out simple LR under-tuning.

**[needs-nuance] — the exact fix (and what NOT to claim).** Add 2–3 sentences in §4.1.2 (or §5.2):
1. State explicitly that the baselines do not merely score *lower* — they sit at the noise floor (~52% final, never above ~55% at any LR), whereas the original reports them learning QNLI.
2. State that both baselines were swept over the **same** learning rates as RoLoRA and never rose above ~55%, so this is **not** under-tuning.
3. Give the mechanism *honestly* as a regime effect: under the reduced 50-client / 20-round / RoBERTa-base proxy, the lossy `avg(AB) ≠ avg(A)avg(B)` interference (Eq. 2) is severe enough that the noisy update never builds coherent signal in the few rounds available; FFA-LoRA is additionally capped by its frozen randomly-oriented down-projection. Tie this to the original's longer budget (RoBERTa-large, 30+ rounds) and to the paper's own scope caveat (only trends transfer).
4. **Do NOT** attribute the collapse to the ADR-0006 shipped-SGD recipe: that was a separate **3-client mech-check** in which RoLoRA *also* sat at chance, so it cannot explain why only the *baselines* collapse in the AdamW Fig-2 runs. The collapse occurs in the already-fixed (AdamW) configuration where RoLoRA reaches 85.1%, so it is a distinct phenomenon. **Do NOT** call the split "IID" — the QNLI proxy is the 50-client heterogeneous regime. **Do NOT** add a binomial "within noise of 50%" sentence — on the ~5,463-example QNLI dev set, 51.9/52.0% is z≈2.8–3.0 above chance (significantly but only marginally so); the existing "barely above the 50% chance level" wording is already correct and should be kept.

### (b) The incomplete init×schedule 2×2 and the unreported orth-A-alone = 82.94 — **gates Novelty**

**The defect.** The paper's most original result is an init×schedule **interaction**, but the 2×2 has a hole and its most diagnostic cell is hidden:

| | Default init | Orthogonal-A init |
|---|---|---|
| **AB (standard alternation)** | 85.10 (n=3, in Table 1) | **82.94 (n=1, OMITTED from Table 1, −2.16 vs vanilla)** |
| **BBA (B-prioritised schedule)** | **NOT RUN (the decisive control)** | 88.32 (n=2, in Table 1) |

Without **default+BBA** you cannot separate a BBA main effect from an orth×BBA interaction. "Orth-A alone hurts but orth-A+BBA is best" is a textbook **interaction signature** — but it remains a *signature*, not a *measured* effect, until the missing cell is filled.

**[needs-nuance] — the exact fix.** The paper already hedges this appropriately (§4.2.2 "promising direction rather than a closed result"; the abstract concedes it "still needs one additional seed and a default-initialisation schedule control"). So this is about **supplying/exposing data**, not retracting an overclaim:
1. **Add the orthogonal-A-alone row to Table 1**, clearly labelled n=1: `Orthogonal A (alone) | 0 | 82.94 (n=1) | −2.16 vs vanilla`. This is the honest negative half of the interaction story and is currently invisible.
2. **Run the default+BBA cell** (≥2 seeds, ideally 3) — this is the single highest-value cheap experiment (~2 runs, ~3h). It converts PC-RoLoRA from "suggestive" to "isolated."
3. In §5.1, state explicitly that the interaction is a *signature*, not a measured effect, because the BBA main effect is unidentified until default+BBA exists. **Do NOT** assert "this is the interaction we report" or call it a verified contribution.
4. A completed 2×2 still would not establish *significance* at n=2 (see (c)) — pair the missing cell with a seed-matched run and a significance statement.

### (c) Table 1 error-bar inconsistency + unestablished significance — **gates Correctness AND Improvements**

**The defect (verified).** Table 1 silently mixes two conventions in one column:

| Variant | Table 1 prints | What it actually is | CI95 (correct, normal-approx 1.96·s/√n) |
|---|---|---|---|
| RoLoRA (n=3) | 85.10 ± **2.97** | **95% CI** | ± 2.97 |
| SVD-compensated (n=3) | 85.70 ± **0.59** | population std | ± 0.83 |
| Orthogonal A + BBA (n=2) | 88.32 ± **0.22** | population std | ± 0.43 |
| Adaptive refresh + orth-A (n=3) | 86.67 ± **0.31** | population std | ± 0.43 |

This makes the improvement arms look ~3–5× tighter than the baseline purely as a convention artifact. **Fig 4 compounds it:** its caption says "95% CI" bands for SVD while the same SVD run in Table 1 reports population std. Seed counts are also inconsistent (n=2 for the headline orth+BBA vs n=3 elsewhere).

**Significance.** orth+BBA 88.32 is n=2 (88.54/88.10); vanilla 85.10 ± 2.97 (CI95) → upper bound ≈ 88.07 ≈ 88.32, i.e. the +3.22pp gain is ≈ the baseline's own CI half-width. A Welch t-test gives t≈2.1, ~2 dof, p≈0.17 — **not significant**, and no test is reported anywhere.

**[needs-nuance] — the exact fix.**
1. **Adopt ONE convention table-wide and state it in the caption.** The panel's recommendation is **95% CI (1.96·s/√n)**, matching the registry house convention (`runs/REGISTRY.md` line 7) and all four figure captions which already say "95% CI." Restate: RoLoRA 85.10 ± 2.97; SVD 85.70 ± 0.83 (recompute from raw seeds — **not** the registry's pre-rounded 0.82); Orth-A+BBA 88.32 ± 0.43; Adaptive 86.67 ± 0.43. *(Note one dissenting reviewer preferred sample-std because a correct small-n CI is t-based and very wide; the panel resolves this in favor of the normal-approx CI95 to match the figures and registry, but the authors should state whichever they pick and apply it uniformly.)*
2. Caption: "± values are 95% CIs (1.96·s/√n) over the seeds listed; n varies by row." After this, Fig 4's "95% CI" band agrees with the SVD ± 0.83 entry.
3. **Flag n=2 at the point of reading:** mark the orth+BBA row "(n=2, preliminary)" so the tightest-looking number is not read as the most settled.
4. **Add one significance sentence** to §4.2.2 after the existing "promising rather than fully verified" caveat: *"With two PC-RoLoRA seeds and three vanilla seeds, a Welch t-test does not establish significance (t≈2.1, ~2 dof, p≈0.17); the +3.2pp gain is comparable to plain RoLoRA's own run-to-run spread, so we report it as suggestive pending a third seed and the default-initialisation+BBA control."* **Do NOT** lean the significance argument on RoLoRA's "88.07 CI upper bound" *before* the convention is unified, since that would compare across mismatched spreads.
5. Light touch on the abstract: change "The strongest proxy result is" → "The most promising (not yet statistically significant) proxy result is." Quote **88.3%** (one decimal) in the abstract to match the surrounding 85.1/85.7/84.0/87.2; reserve 88.32 for Table 1.

### (d) Missing reproducibility audit — **the single most valuable reproduction finding, left in the repo**

**The defect.** §3.2 says only "we used the code released by the RoLoRA authors, together with their default experimental configuration" — but the team never ran the shipped defaults to get their numbers, and never reports that the shipped config does not learn. ADR 0006 documents a first-class reproduction finding entirely absent from the 8-page PDF.

**Verified facts (ADR 0006 / `runs/REGISTRY.md` §3).** The supplement's only QNLI config `test_glue.yaml` ships **SGD lr=0.005** (Adam line commented out, line 74); under it all three modes sit at chance (rolora 0.5162 / lora 0.5213 / ffa 0.5193) after ~39 rounds, whereas **AdamW lr=5e-4** reaches 0.86–0.88 (0.8766 / 0.8783 / 0.8607). There is an **undocumented SEQ_CLS classifier head frozen from step 0** (no flag/comment), measured to cost <0.01 absolute accuracy (control 0.8688). There is **no public GitHub** for the federated paper (the `huangowen/rolora` repo is an unrelated quantization paper; the OpenReview supplement is the only artifact).

**The exact fix.** Add a **"Reproducibility audit of the OpenReview supplement"** subsection (main body if space, otherwise appendix — W8 explicitly welcomes appendices, and the exemplar was rewarded for its "Challenges Encountered" section). Required content, framed with ADR 0006's two-tier strong/weak distinction:
- **(strong)** The shipped recipe is SGD lr=0.005; Table 6 underspecifies the optimizer; present the SGD-vs-AdamW table with the scale stated (**RoBERTa-base, 3-client IID, ~40-round mech-check**) so it is not confused with the 50-client proxy. State it confirms only the SGD-vs-AdamW story and **does NOT confirm or refute the method ranking** at this scale.
- **(weak / code-quality)** The undocumented SEQ_CLS freeze, with its measured <0.01 cost — frame as surprising/unmotivated, **NOT** as the cause of chance accuracy.
- **(artifact)** The no-public-GitHub finding.
- **Most important for correctness:** rewrite the §3.2 "default experimental configuration" sentence to state truthfully that the reported 85.1% was obtained **NOT** with the shipped SGD defaults but with an LR override (lr1e-2) plus two trainer patches (classifier-unfreeze; alternation-scope/step_count fix), and that the SLS_DEBUG_GRAD probe confirms the alternation is exact once eval-mode step_count drift is fixed.
- **Do NOT claim** "the published code cannot learn" (the AdamW control refutes it), "the alternation logic is broken" (the grad probe refutes it), or use this audit to explain the §4.1.2 baseline collapse (see (a)).

## 4. Paste-ready fixes

### 4.1 §1 Contributions paragraph (insert at end of §1.6)

```latex
\paragraph{Contributions.} We (i) reproduce RoLoRA's robustness claim at two
scales---a re-implemented two-layer MNIST toy model and a deliberately reduced
RoBERTa-base/QNLI proxy using the authors' released code---recovering the
qualitative ordering (RoLoRA $\gg$ FedAvg-LoRA, FFA-LoRA) at both; (ii) map an
\emph{init\,$\times$\,schedule} design space the original RoLoRA ablation
(schedule-only, default init) never crosses, and report that our strongest proxy
configuration, orthogonal-$A$ initialisation with a $B$-prioritised (BBA)
schedule, reaches $88.3\%$ (n{=}2) versus $85.1\%$ vanilla, while orthogonal-$A$
\emph{alone} falls below vanilla on the proxy ($82.94\%$, single seed)---a
pattern suggestive of an init$\times$schedule interaction that we report as a
promising but not-yet-established direction (PC-RoLoRA), since it still lacks the
decisive default-initialisation$+$BBA control and additional seeds; (iii) show
that RoLoRA \emph{composes selectively}: subspace-conditioning extensions help,
whereas update-level modifications (LoRA+ per-matrix learning rates, FedProx
proximal updates) do not; and (iv) audit the reproducibility of the released
artifact and release all code, configs, and per-seed run logs.
```

### 4.2 §3.x Reproducibility-audit subsection

```latex
\subsection{Reproducibility Audit of the Released Artifact}
The original federated paper has no public code repository; the OpenReview
supplement is the only released artifact (the similarly named public
\texttt{rolora} repository is an unrelated quantization paper). Auditing this
supplement surfaced two issues we report as reproduction findings.

\textbf{Optimizer/learning-rate gap (primary).} The supplement's sole QNLI
configuration, \texttt{federatedscope/llm/baseline/test\_glue.yaml}, ships with
\textsc{SGD} at $\eta=0.005$ (the AdamW line is commented out, line 74), and the
paper's hyperparameter table does not pin the optimizer. In a centralized-style
mechanism check (RoBERTa-base, 3 IID clients, 40 rounds) all three modes remain
at chance under this recipe (RoLoRA $0.516$, LoRA $0.521$, FFA-LoRA $0.519$),
whereas switching to AdamW $\eta=5\!\times\!10^{-4}$ recovers learning to
$0.86$--$0.88$ ($0.877$ / $0.878$ / $0.861$). This confirms the SGD-vs-AdamW
reproducibility story only; at this reduced scale it neither confirms nor refutes
the paper's method ranking.

\textbf{Undocumented classifier freeze (secondary, code-quality).} The trainer
permanently freezes the freshly initialised \texttt{SEQ\_CLS} head from step $0$,
with no documentation or flag. We measure its cost at $<\!0.01$ absolute test
accuracy ($0.8688$ frozen vs $0.8766$ unfrozen); it is a surprising, unmotivated
setting rather than the cause of the chance-level behaviour above.

\textbf{Consequence for our runs.} All QNLI numbers reported in this paper were
therefore obtained \emph{not} with the shipped SGD defaults but with AdamW, a
learning-rate override (the swept set below), classifier unfreezing, and a
minimal alternation-scope/step-count patch; a gradient probe confirms the
alternation remains exact once an eval-mode step-count drift is corrected.
```

rank 4, learning rate $10^{-2}$. Values are final-round server test accuracy,

listed; $n$ varies by row. The headline Orthogonal $A$ $+$ BBA row is

observation.}

The report's "Team contributions" paragraph was self-authored (by D. Popovici)
and is the hard-gate rubric item. We audited it against the repository record.

**Original text.** *"Daniel Popovici led the initial report structure, reproduction
setup, results interpretation, and toy/baseline analysis. Vlad Iftode led the
improvement implementation and runs, including the language-model proxy
experiments. Sorin Zele contributed to the proposal and report writing,
presentation/report integration, final editing, feedback incorporation, and
submission coordination."*

**Repository evidence (git authorship).** Vlad Iftode 51 commits (two emails),
Daniel Popovici 11 (all 2026-05-20 → 06-01), Sorin Zele 0 (no repo footprint;
appears only in author lists — his work is in Overleaf/slides, invisible to git).

| Claim | Verdict vs evidence |
|---|---|
| Daniel — "toy/baseline analysis" | ✅ accurate (his commits: toy notebook, baseline + orthogonal-A toy results, plots) |
| Daniel — "reproduction setup" | ⚠️ partly supported (he authored SLURM/queue scripts + wandb wiring + setup-script fix) — but "setup" ≠ the reproduction itself |
| Daniel — "initial report structure" | ✅ confirmed (Daniel made the initial draft) |
| Daniel — "results interpretation" | ❓ vague/unverifiable; dropped in the rewrite |
| Vlad — "improvement implementation and runs" | ❌ **badly undersells**: omits the proxy reproduction *execution*, the LR sweeps, the **reproducibility audit** (the panel's strongest reproduction finding — credited to no one), and the consolidated run registry — all overwhelmingly his per git |
| Sorin — six soft items | ❓ entirely unverifiable from the repo (0 commits); plausible (Overleaf/slides) but the team must confirm |

**Problem.** It is mis-weighted, not fabricated: vague "led" verbs frame the
early-phase author as project-wide technical lead, the heaviest *verifiable* lift
(reproduction execution + audit + registry) is compressed into one clause, and
the biggest single piece of work (the reproducibility audit) is uncredited.

\paragraph{Team contributions.} Daniel Popovici produced the initial report
draft and structure, built the reproduction scaffolding (SLURM/queue submission
scripts, Weights \& Biases logging, environment setup), and implemented the
MNIST toy model with its baseline and orthogonal-$A$ experiments and

improvement variants (orthogonal-$A$ initialisation, the BBA schedule,

learning-rate sweeps; he also performed the reproducibility audit of the
released artifact and assembled the consolidated run registry and aggregation
tooling behind the reported numbers. Sorin Zele led the proposal and report
writing, the presentation, report/presentation integration, final editing,
feedback incorporation, and submission coordination.

## 7. Grounding caveat — how much of this review is verified

This panel was a **verification-and-prioritisation pass over a pre-supplied
defect list**, not an independent fresh read of the paper. Each reviewer was
seeded with a ground-truth block that already named the major defects (the
"facts reviewers should weaponize"), and verifiers were told to open the PDF
only when a claim hinged on wording they couldn't confirm from the summary. So
the panel is reliable where it rests on `runs/REGISTRY.md` / ADR-0006 raw
numbers, and weaker where it makes claims about *external* facts. Grounding
status of the load-bearing claims:

| Claim in this review | Grounding | Status |
|---|---|---|
| All per-seed proxy numbers, 2×2 cells, error-bar recomputations, LR sweeps | `runs/REGISTRY.md` raw logs | ✅ verified |
| Reproducibility-audit numbers (0.8766 / 0.8688 / 0.8607; SGD ~0.52) | ADR-0006 table | ✅ verified |
| `5·10⁻⁵` typo, "19 rounds", and prose quotes ("strongest proxy result"; "promising direction rather than a closed result"; "needs one additional seed and a default-initialisation schedule control") | paper text (`pdftotext`), spot-checked | ✅ verified — quotes are accurate |
| Significance tests | **recomputed from raw seeds** | ✅ verified: main Welch **t=2.10, df=2.08, p=0.166**; toy Welch **t=3.05, p=0.019**, paired **t=2.57, p=0.062**, variance **F=2.44** (sd 2.04pp → 1.31pp) — review's figures were correct, not hallucinated |
| Original-paper anchor RoLoRA QNLI 50-client | original paper Table 1 | ✅ verified = **90.00 ± 0.63** (review wrote ±0.61 — **fix the decimal**) |
| **"Baselines collapse contradicts the original (which learns QNLI)"** | original paper Table 1 | ⚠️ **OVER-STATED — reframe (see below)** |
| FedSA-LoRA citation (ICLR 2025, Pengxin-Guo) / arXiv 2410.01463 | web-verified | ✅ verified: Guo et al., *Selective Aggregation for Low-Rank Adaptation in Federated Learning*, ICLR 2025, **arXiv:2410.01463** — id and venue are correct |

**The one real correction — baseline-collapse framing.** The original paper's
Table 1 (RoBERTa-**Large** 355M, **best** test accuracy over an **8-point LR
sweep** {5e-4 … 1e-1}, full participation) reports, at **50 clients**:

| 50-client | LoRA | FFA-LoRA | RoLoRA |
|---|---|---|---|
| QNLI | 78.13 ± 5.13 | 85.05 ± 0.34 | 90.00 ± 0.63 |
| MNLI | **52.64 ± 15.07 (≈ chance!)** | 69.97 ± 5.57 | 85.28 ± 1.04 |

So "the original's baselines *learn* QNLI" is only half true: the original's own
50-client baselines are **already degrading hard** — LoRA QNLI is 78 % with a
±5 spread, and LoRA on 50-client **MNLI sits at 52.6 % (chance) with ±15
variance.** Our collapse therefore **amplifies a trend the original itself
shows**; it does not flatly contradict it. The correct §4.1.2/§5.2 framing (and
it is *more* favourable to the report): *"The original observes the same
direction — at 50 clients its LoRA baseline is already unstable (QNLI 78 ± 5)
and collapses to chance on MNLI (52.6 ± 15). Our harsher proxy — RoBERTa-base
(125M) vs Large, final-round vs best-over-sweep accuracy, and a 20-round budget
— pushes the QNLI baselines to the floor as well; this is amplified regime
fragility, not a discrepancy."* This also supplies the apples-to-oranges caveat
roadmap #15 wants: the original reports **best-over-8-LRs on RoBERTa-Large**, we
report **final-round on RoBERTa-base**.

| C8 | NIT | §2.3 / Alg 1 | Algorithm 1 loops "**for t = 0, 2, 4, …, T**" while labelling its first inner step "**Odd phase: update B**" (t is even); the round/cycle index vs. the odd/even-round prose is internally confusing, and the upload/broadcast lines (4, 9) are split mid-step. | Make the loop index match the "odd round = B, even round = A" prose, or relabel to "phase 1 / phase 2 of cycle t". |
| C9 | MINOR | Abstract | The abstract **leads with the (weaker) improvement numbers and never states the strongest, cleanest result** — the reproduction gap (baselines collapse to ~52%, RoLoRA 85.1%, ~33 pp). Reproduction is 10/60 and this is the most defensible finding. | Add one sentence to the abstract stating the reproduced gap before the improvement results. |

**Bottom line on the cold read:** no new *blocker* — the panel's primed list did
catch the grade-gating issues. But the close read found a **second flattened-
superscript typo (C1, λ≈2⁴)**, a **broken/informal sentence (C2)**, and three
real structural wins (**C3** §5/§6 duplication, **C4** baselines absent from any
table, **C9** abstract omits the reproduction headline) — all cheap, all in the
"Report quality 15/60" correctness/completeness bucket. These are additive to the
Tier-0 list in §5.
